items.title: Context paragraph
items.body:
On 18 August 2025 I moved to a team with limited overlap with my Team Leader, so guidance during calls was often sought through group chats or other supervisors.

The cases above highlight different Ofcom regulatory concerns that arose while handling customer issues.

These examples appear in my disclosure dossier; additional cases and detailed analysis are provided there. The evidence consists primarily of contemporaneous Microsoft Teams screenshots.

items.title: Silence Treated as Consent to Contract
items.body: After a customer stated they had not consented to a contract, I was instructed consent was verifiable if the customer’s record showed a contract email had been sent. Ofcom requires verifiable express consent.
items.source_text_exact:

items.title: TL Closed Complaint Despite Customer Instruction
items.body: Complaint closed suddenly despite the customer stating it should remain open until the issue was resolved. Ofcom requires complaints remain open until the customer considers it resolved.
items.source_text_exact:

items.title: Translator Refused and ADR Blocked
items.body: A vulnerable customer stated a debt with a collection agency resulted from a language barrier. No evidence could be located. I was instructed to inform the customer the debt stood and close the complaint without mentioning Alternative Dispute Resolution. Ofcom requires access to ADR where complaints remain unresolved.

items.title: Complaints Training
items.body: WebEx “Back to Basics” training promoted rapid complaint closure and adviser-led resolution. Compliance concerns: alignment with Ofcom GC C4 requirements for complaint resolution and ADR access. Full analysis in dossier.

items.title: Vulnerable Customer Escalation
items.body: 85-year-old widow reported a store visit had resulted in a more expensive package. After a repeated humiliating in-store experience, she refused to return. Escalation resulted in the Team Leader overlooking vulnerability, offering no resolution, and closing the complaint without permission - preventing access to ADR. Ofcom requires adjusted support to safeguard vulnerable customers.

Some lower-lane/internal-process items may be visually grouped near September/November material in the source layout, but only explicitly stated dates should control exact anchoring.

The 11 Nov GH-04 received marker belongs to the visible Phase 2 handoff zone on the Phase 1 page and should be rendered as continuation material, not absorbed into the Phase 1 date range.
